title: Basket Analysis Without Superstition
objective: After this lesson you will be able to mine item co-occurrence pairs with support/confidence gates, validate rules on holdout baskets, and reject high-confidence rare rules as noise.
why: 'Customers who buy X also buy Y' drives bundles, placement, and recommendations — and also drives nonsense when rare coincidences get promoted. Support × confidence gating plus holdout validation separates patterns from coincidences: rules earn deployment by surviving unseen baskets, not by impressing in-sample.

blocks.text: **Support** (fraction of baskets containing both items) measures evidence volume; **confidence** (P(Y|X)) measures rule strength. High confidence with tiny support is anecdote with math (2 co-buys from 2 chances). Gate both: minimum support (evidence exists) AND minimum confidence (strength matters). Either alone admits noise — together they admit patterns.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
from itertools import combinations
csv = "basket,item\n1,shoes\n1,socks\n2,shoes\n2,socks\n3,shoes\n3,hat\n4,socks\n4,hat\n"
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv))
baskets = df.groupby("basket")["item"].apply(set)
N = len(baskets)
pairs = {}
for b in baskets:
    for a, c in combinations(sorted(b), 2):
        pairs[(a, c)] = pairs.get((a, c), 0) + 1
rules = []
for (a, c), n in pairs.items():
    sup = n / N
    conf = n / sum(1 for b in baskets if a in b)
    if sup >= 0.25 and conf >= 0.5:
        rules.append(((a, c), round(sup, 2), round(conf, 2)))
print("rules:", rules)

blocks.text: Holdout validation: patterns survive unseen baskets

Split baskets (not rows) into mine/validate sets: rules mined on one half must hold (support × confidence rechecked) on the other. In-sample-only rules overfit coincidence — holdout is where superstition dies. Report both halves' numbers; large gaps mean the 'pattern' was sampling noise.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
from itertools import combinations
csv = "basket,item\n1,shoes\n1,socks\n2,shoes\n2,socks\n3,shoes\n3,hat\n4,socks\n4,hat\n"
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv))
mine = df[df["basket"].isin([1, 2])]
hold = df[df["basket"].isin([3, 4])]

def pair_support(frame):
    b = frame.groupby("basket")["item"].apply(set)
    d, n = {}, len(b)
    for s in b:
        for a, c in combinations(sorted(s), 2):
            d[(a, c)] = d.get((a, c), 0) + 1
    return {k: v / n for k, v in d.items()}

print("mine:", pair_support(mine))
print("holdout:", pair_support(hold))

blocks.title: Gate the rules
blocks.note: Run it: gated keeps shoes|socks (s=0.5, c≈0.67); strict (0.5/0.9) keeps nothing — gates decide what exists. Same data, different standards, different rule sets: thresholds are policy.

items: Support (evidence volume) × confidence (rule strength) gates together — either alone admits noise
Holdout baskets validate: mine on half, recheck on half; gaps expose coincidence
Thresholds are policy (business cost of false bundles), not statistics

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice gater on both thresholds and map surviving rules. (b) In Python (your env), run both lesson snippets and confirm mine/holdout supports. (c) State the business cost of a false bundle rule (wrong cross-sell) vs a missed rule, and how gates encode the trade.
hints: Twin outputs: gated keeps shoes|socks; strict keeps nothing (0.5/0.9 kills all four-basket evidence).
Python: mine supports vs holdout supports per pair (small data, visible numbers).
False bundles waste placement/promotion spend and erode trust; missed rules cost opportunity silently — gates set by promotion economics, reviewed per campaign.
exercise.why: Threshold-as-policy (gates decide rule sets), holdout discipline (coincidence dies unseen baskets), and cost framing (false bundles vs missed rules) are the three association judgments.
exercise.code: # Association pattern: support × confidence gates + holdout recheck, always.

quiz.q: Rule with 100% confidence from 2 baskets. Deploy?
options: No: support 2/N fails evidence gates — high-confidence rare rules are noise until holdout-validated at scale
quiz.explain: Confidence without support is anecdote with math. Gates require evidence volume AND strength, validated on unseen baskets.

options: Coincidence exposed: in-sample pattern fails unseen data — reject or re-mine with stricter gates
quiz.explain: Divergence falsifies the pattern: it was sampling noise, not signal. Holdout exists precisely to kill such rules.

options: Business economics per campaign (promotion cost vs opportunity) — thresholds are policy, reviewed per use
quiz.explain: Gates price false positives vs false negatives in campaign terms. Fixed universal thresholds misprice most applications.

summary: Support × confidence gates, holdout validation, thresholds as campaign policy. Patterns earn deployment by surviving unseen baskets.
